newsitem.title: USA: Clarke Cty, Ga., to sell $45 mln GO issue in May.
newsitem.headline: Clarke Cty, Ga., to sell $45 mln GO issue in May.

text.p: Georgia's Clarke County School District plans to sell $45 million of general obligation bonds the first week in May, issue underwriter A.G. Edwards & Sons said Friday.
The noncallable issue will have serials out to five years, A.G. Edwards Vice President Todd Barnes said.
The issue includes $4 million of current refunding of the school district's 1987 bond issue.
Debt service will be paid with a one-cent local-option sales tax approved by voters in March. The tax takes effect July 1 and will last five years.
In addition to the debt service on the new issue, the tax is expected to raise $18 million to retire the school district's 1993 bond issue and to raise about $20 million for pay-as-you go projects.

Clarke was one of 63 Georgia counties that adopted the local-option sales tax after voters approved a constitutional amendment authorizing the tax in November. The amendment allows school districts to use the tax revenue for capital projects and to retire oustanding debt.
The school district is rated single-A by Moody's Investors Service and A-plus by Standard & Poor's Corp.

Barnes said the rating could be raised if the school district participates in the state's revenue intercept program. Under that program, the state education department intercepts part of school districts' state funding and automatically transfers their debt service payments to the paying agents.
Moody's Investors Service rated that program Aa3 earlier this month, and said it would assign the same rating to qualifying bond issues by districts that participate.
